<h2 id="homepage-name">Jen Jordan</h2>

**PhD Candidate, Environmental Science and Policy**  
[George Mason University](https://science.gmu.edu/academics/departments-units/environmental-science-policy){target="_blank"} · [Forkner Plant–Insect Lab](https://rebeccaeforkner.wixsite.com/rebeccaeforkner/the-lab){target="_blank"}

**Predoctoral Fellow**  
[Smithsonian Conservation Biology Institute](https://nationalzoo.si.edu/conservation){target="_blank"} · [ForestGEO Ecosystems and Climate Program](https://ecoclimlab.github.io){target="_blank"}

My research examines how climate extremes and disturbance affect tree growth and woody carbon accumulation in eastern temperate forests. My dissertation integrates tree-growth records, field measurements, and canopy productivity data to investigate how heat, atmospheric drought, and structural damage constrain forest carbon storage.

[Research](research.qmd){target="_blank"} · [Publications](publications.qmd){target="_blank"} · [Download CV](Jen_Jordan_CV.pdf){target="_blank"} · [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5521-360X){target="_blank"} · [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jen-jordan-forest){target="_blank"} · [GitHub](https://github.com/jenajordan){target="_blank"}

## Research Themes

**Climate Extremes and Forest Growth**

How the timing, duration, and persistence of extreme heat and atmospheric drought affect woody growth.

**Carbon Uptake and Woody Biomass**

When canopy carbon uptake and long-lived woody biomass accumulation diverge under climate stress.

**Forest Disturbance and Resilience**

How non-lethal crown damage influences tree growth and stand-level forest productivity.

[Learn more about my research →](research.qmd)
